carnage.name: 3_vodkas_in
carnage.commentary: Saved the ugliest for later: a 5 on a par 3 with no shot trace to hide behind, then another 5 on the 16th that netted out to a 6. The card says two doubles showed up anyway, and the short game was bleeding bad enough (-3.14 SG) that even a strong putting day couldn’t fully bandage it.

carnage.name: Factor_Golf
carnage.commentary: This one had all the charm of a parking-lot airball: a 5 on the 2nd with no shot sequence logged, and then the rest of the round kept feeding the fire. Five 3-putts and -6.62 putting is how you turn a decent 10 GIR into a dumpster fire.

carnage.name: GeTGolf
carnage.commentary: The first hole came in as a 4 with no shot detail, which is a soft way to start a round and not the last time the card bit back. The real damage on the worst-hole list is still just that opening bogey, because the rest of the damage was more drip-feed than one giant crash.

carnage.name: Golfnut7413
carnage.commentary: A 4 on the 4th with no shot detail was the headline bogey, which is annoyingly boring for a guy whose stats were otherwise doing some work. The bigger problem was the pile of five bogeys around a nice little 6-birdie card, because golf loves to make “pretty good” look stupid.

carnage.name: AdamH05
carnage.commentary: The 3rd-hole bogey was the worst hole, and the scorecard politely declines to explain how it happened. That’s fitting for a round that had enough tidy stretches to keep the wreckage modest, but not enough precision to stop three bogeys from showing up and mugging the card.

carnage.name: Jonty
carnage.commentary: The worst hole was a clean 3 on the opening par 3, because apparently the card was already running out of ways to punish him. No shot data, no blow-up sequence, just a scorecard that somehow says -6 gross and still drags him to +10 net like the format had a personal grudge.

players.name: AdamH05
players.tagline: Hit enough greens to tease competence, then putted like the cup owed him money.
players.body: Net had him buried at +7, while the gross card was only +1, so the league format absolutely did him dirty compared with the raw score. The underlying profile was weirdly split: approach got clipped at -2.21, short game actually helped at +1.89, and putting chipped in +0.82, but none of that overcame 29 putts, a lone 3-putt, and just 2 birdies against 3 bogeys. He did pop a couple of par-3 birdies at 9 and 12, but the run of bogey-ish par-3s at 3, 6, and 10 kept the round from ever threatening anything. With no prior starts on record, this is just the current round talking, and it says he found enough good shots to avoid disaster, but not enough of them to keep the net card from wandering into the weeds.

players.name: Golfnut7413
players.tagline: Gross was solid enough; the net card still found a way to stomp on the tires.
players.body: He finished +7 net and -1 gross, which is the kind of split that says the ball was in play often enough to matter, but the format still handed him the short end. The data says the engine was real: +2.12 approach, +1.94 putting, and 22 total putts with zero 3-putts, so the flatstick actually showed up for once. But the round also coughed up five bogeys, and that’s how a guy can make 6 birdies, hit 9 greens, and still look like he left money on the table. The worst hole was the 4th, one of a cluster of par-3 bogeys around 4, 5, and 6 that kept the card from catching fire. With no prior starts to lean on, this is just one round’s worth of evidence, but the raw golf says the pieces were there; the scoring just didn’t stay glued together.

players.name: 3_vodkas_in
players.tagline: Made enough birdies to look alive, then stapled on two doubles like he was trying to finish the job.
players.body: The net finish was +7, same as the other guys in the mud, but the gross card at +2 was a little less ugly than the net result suggests. The stat line is a weird little cocktail: -3.14 short game and -3.38 tee to green, but +2.88 putting and 99 feet of putts made, which is basically “everything broke except the part that gets the ball in the hole.” That said, two double bogeys and only 4 birdies is a nasty trade when the rest of the field is also leaking bogeys. The ugly spots were the 11th and 16th, with the 11th serving as the worst hole at a 5 and the 16th adding another messy 5-to-6 net sequence. No prior starts means no trend to sell here, just a round that had enough putter to survive and enough tee-to-green noise to keep it from ever becoming something better.

players.name: GeTGolf
players.tagline: The short game carried the whole bag while the rest of it wandered around like it missed curfew.
players.body: He landed at +8 net and -2 gross, which is a classic “the raw score was decent but the format still said go sit in the corner” situation. The gross side was propped up by 4 birdies and only 2 bogeys, and the SG split tells the same story in louder language: +4.79 around the greens and +3.93 tee to green with a slightly negative putter at -0.44. The ugly part is the green-in-regulation total, just 7, because that kind of scrambling is a high-wire act, not a plan. The worst hole was the opening 1st, a bogey start, and the first two holes were both 4s before the round steadied. With no history to compare it to, the clean read is simple: the short game saved a bunch of mess, but the round was still too choppy to escape the net bogey swamp.

players.name: Factor_Golf
players.tagline: Five 3-putts and zero birdies is a brutal little art project.
players.body: The card was an outright disaster: +10 net, +10 gross, and a gross SG total of -8.5 that looks like the putter got mugged behind the clubhouse. He actually hit 10 greens, which makes the 36 putts, five 3-putts, and zero birdies even uglier, because that’s not bad ball-striking so much as a complete failure to cash the check. The worst hole was the 2nd, a 5 on a par 3, but the real villain was the broader putting collapse at -6.62 SG. Three double-bogey-or-worse holes sealed the vibe, and the round never recovered after the early damage. With no prior starts to compare against, this is just one brutal receipt: the ball found enough greens to imply a pulse, and then the putter immediately called the coroner.

players.name: Jonty
players.tagline: Gross went off, net still kicked him in the shins. That’s golf math being a dick.
players.body: He posted a +10 net and a -6 gross, which is exactly the kind of split that makes the format feel like it’s throwing elbows. The raw numbers were loud in the good direction: +4.36 approach, +3.08 short game, and +7.43 tee to green, with 13 greens in regulation and no bogeys or doubles on the gross card. The putter was basically neutral at +0.07, so this wasn’t a putting rescue act; it was ball-striking and short-game control doing the heavy lifting. Still, the net card got blunted, and the scorebook shows a bunch of net-par holes turning into net bogeys, including the 3rd and a couple more on the early stretch. The worst hole was the opening 1st, a plain 3 on a par 3, which tells you how tame the actual blow-up evidence was in the scorecard. No prior starts means no trend line yet, but the current round says he had one of the best raw performances in this batch and still got mugged by the net math.
